observation.visible_scene: Night scene at a beach: a large fireworks burst dominates the upper-center sky above a dark water line, with a distant city skyline of small lights along the horizon. Silhouetted spectators occupy the foreground sand, including a standing couple near the center and a denser crowd at the lower left; the bright burst casts a shifting golden reflection on the water.
visible_changes: The fireworks burst is already mid-explosion at t=0 and continues to expand radially throughout the clip; its center stays roughly fixed in the upper-center of the frame while the streaks spread outward rather than translating across the sky.

Early frames show a gold/orange crown over a magenta-purple core; as the sequence progresses additional golden bursts merge into the center, and the core grows into an overwhelmingly bright white-yellow mass (peaking around t=0.8–1.6s).

After the bright peak, the central glow softens and the periphery resolves into discrete purple/blue droplet-like stars that hang and slowly drift downward, fading as smoke accumulates on the left side of the burst.
The water reflection brightens and dims in step with the burst intensity, and the smoke plume near the horizon thickens over time.

A blurred foreground head/silhouette enters from the bottom edge around t=1.1s and shifts position across the lower frame (appearing to pass in front of the camera), while the standing couple and skyline remain in fixed positions.
The background horizon and city lights stay at constant frame positions, indicating no significant camera pan; the apparent motion is the firework's own expansion and the foreground silhouette.
outside_clip_unknowns: The shell launch and the final complete dissipation of the burst lie outside this excerpt; the clip begins and ends with the explosion still in progress.
Whether other fireworks were fired before t=0 or after t=3.2s is not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact movement of the foreground silhouette (walking vs. a head bobbing) cannot be confirmed; it is an occlusion change, not part of the firework.
Minor frame-to-frame brightness differences could include slight camera exposure variation rather than pure firework change.
The relative depth between the couple and the entering silhouette is not precisely determinable.
